To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
foreign aid to education does not promote gender equality in developing country education systems, except at the primary level where it has a positive impact.
aid disbursements in the education sector have a negative impact on gender parity at the secondary and the tertiary education levels, but have no impact on parity in primary education.

aid in the education sector does not foster gender equality in enrolment at primary education level, but does negatively affect gender equality in enrolments at the secondary and post-secondary education levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of foreign education aid on gender equality.
the impact of foreign assistance to education in developing countries and the extent to which it promotes gender equality in education.
the effects of foreign aid on education outcomes in developing and emerging countries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
foreign aid in education does not foster gender equality in education.
foreign aid to education does not foster gender equality in education in developing countries.
aid to education does not foster gender equality in education in developing countries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
foreign aid to the education sector has no impact on gender equality in developing country education outcomes.
foreign aid in education has a negative impact on gender parity at the secondary and higher education levels.
foreign aid in education is not a panacea for gender equality in education.

foreign aid in education does not promote gender equality.
aid to education does not necessarily foster gender equality in education.
aid to the education sector does not seem to foster gender equality in enrolment in developing countries.
